name: FR-13 development thread set (step 7 phase 3)
status: DEVELOPMENT SET, NOT FROZEN. Drafted 8 November 2026 for step 7 phase 3 (D-93): the set the follow-up-focus changes are TUNED on, so it is never a test set and no result from it is reported as a measurement of FR-13. Drafted from the corpus files and the indexed chunks only; the frozen sets' files were not read, and the identifier-only overlap check (runs/2026-11-08/fr13-phase3-dev/) is the evidence of separation. Worded as users talk, with pronouns and ellipsis that need the earlier question.
corpus: The Objective 02 corpus, exactly as indexed from corpus/objective-02/manifest.json on kmp_obj02_20261101: 20 documents and 5 transcripts in 43 chunks. The scoped threads turn to D15 and D16, deliberately not the frozen set's D09 and T02.
notes: Two turns per thread: scripts/thread_set.py validates exactly two (D-86), so the brief's '2 to 3 turns' resolves to two.
Twelve threads: eight ordinary, two scoped asked by both roles, one topic change, one previous-answer follow-up (expected to fail with history, D-86 decision 2).
Thread ids start at t20 so no run id can be mistaken for the frozen set's t01-t09.
The previous-answer follow-up refers to a fact the first ANSWER introduces (inactivity), not the first question; under D-42 the reference should not resolve.
http_check entries exist because validation requires them; this set is run in-process only and the HTTP check stays on the frozen set.

Extended 9 November 2026 for step 7 phase 4 (D-103's 'before any further attempt'): t32-t38 are CROSS-SOURCE threads - each follow-up's expected source is a DIFFERENT manifest item from turn 1's, the composition the 8 November set lacked (8 of its 10 answerable follow-ups kept their source inside turn 1's item, so it could not detect a fix to the frozen failure mode). Six ordinary and one scoped, ids continuing from t31. Drafted from the corpus files only; the frozen sets' files were again not read, and the identifier-only overlap check (phase 2a's thresholds) was re-run over the whole extended set.

scoring_rule.applies_to: Every run of every thread, all four ways, scored by the same rule as the frozen set.
parts: The rule is version 2 as implemented in scripts/thread_set.py, the same code path the frozen set is scored with: one outcome class per run; the expected-answer match is a listed phrase (substring, whitespace collapsed, case folded) or an accepted alternative (whole tokens), plus a cited listed source; a leak is an out-of-scope chunk, an out-of-scope partial match, or a restricted phrase in a role's verified statements. The canonical prose of the rule is frozen with corpus/objective-02/threads.json and is not restated here; this set exists to be scored by the same functions, not to redefine them.
